source_review.notes: Checked the final OMG SysML 2.0 Language and v1-to-v2 Transformation specifications, final KerML 1.0 and Systems Modeling API and Services 1.0 specifications, their current OMG specification pages and normative artifact listings, the current OMG Systems Modeling Community release repository, active NASA-HDBK-1009A, and the active IEEE/ISO/IEC 42010-2022 catalog record. Nine URLs returned HTTP 200 directly; the ISO catalog initially returned HTTP 403 to curl despite successful browser retrieval, so the final reference uses the IEEE Standards Association page, which returned HTTP 200. Claims distinguish 2025 formal adoption from the March 2026 editorial publications and do not use beta syntax as normative guidance.

evidence: Reviewed the versioned typed-graph model M_c=(E,R,T,N,L,V,c) and confirmed every symbol is defined in place.
Reviewed set interpretations for usage typing and feature subsetting and confirmed they express constraint rather than object creation or evidence of existence.
Reviewed element, feature, connection and query records for identity, ownership, version, applicability and evidence conditions.
Confirmed multiplicity, typing and connection compatibility are not presented as proof of availability, physical feasibility or system performance.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation is explanatory and project-check oriented; it does not claim to reproduce the complete normative KerML or SysML formal semantics.

evidence: Executed declared-sysml-semantics-check using python3 with the exact expected output recorded in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-056/report.json.
Confirmed four declarations, five usages, five unique qualified usage names, five resolved usage types and five nonempty owners.
Confirmed two port usages, one connection, compatible ElectricPower item declarations at both endpoints, two requirements, two verification-case mappings and zero uncovered requirements.
Confirmed the checker emits evidence=declared_subset_only and does not claim OMG language conformance, verification execution or physical compatibility.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable evidence is a deterministic data-integrity demonstration, not a parser, solver, model repository or conformance suite.

evidence: Confirmed typed usage inclusion is consistent with the stated classifier interpretation.
Confirmed feature subsetting is represented as value-set containment and is not conflated with feature typing, redefinition, binding or dependency.
Confirmed the connection predicate explicitly conjoins type, direction, multiplicity, mode, configuration and domain evidence rather than treating one relation as sufficient.
Confirmed query results are parameterized by model commit and reproducibility conditions so branch-head drift is not mistaken for a logical contradiction.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No claim is made that the simplified predicates are a complete axiomatization of SysML 2.0.

evidence: Challenged language-versus-method, model-versus-diagram, architecture-versus-description, syntax-versus-semantics and validation-versus-real-system evidence boundaries.
Reviewed definition/usage confusion, same-name identity collision, unresolved imports, library drift, incorrect specialization/subsetting/redefinition/binding and composite occurrence ambiguity.
Reviewed endpoint direction/item/multiplicity/mode/configuration mismatch, port conjugation limits and missing electrical, mechanical, protocol, timing, safety and security evidence.
Reviewed calculated point margin, satisfaction assertions, verification-case coverage, execution verdicts, inconclusive results, and circular requirement evidence.
Reviewed viewpoint exclusions, copied view values, generated-document provenance, authored versus derived facts and tool-specific extension loss.
Reviewed API pagination, authorization filtering, invalid commits, partial failures, schema evolution, stable identity, round trips and misleading image-level equivalence.
Reviewed v1 profiles, opaque behaviors, scripts, validation rules, source-target traces, unmapped content, golden analyses and premature source retirement.
Reviewed all ten worked examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limits and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Consequential models still require applicable domain, architecture, human-factors, physical-interface, safety, security, assurance, tool-conformance, verification, validation and decision-authority review.

evidence: Traced formal language, KerML, libraries, API/schema, transformation and tool versions throughout authoring, query, interchange and migration guidance.
Confirmed identity, name, qualified name, ownership/membership, typing, source, status, configuration and version remain distinct.
Confirmed configuration compatibility is required across requirements, usages, ports, behavior, properties, cases and evidence.
Confirmed requirements, satisfaction assertions, verification specifications, executions and verdicts retain separate identities and evidence states.
Confirmed views are reproducible from a commit/viewpoint/rendering rule and cannot silently redefine exposed semantic content.
Confirmed derived/implied facts remain reproducible and distinguishable from authored facts.
Confirmed every in-scope migration item must be transformed, mapped, retained as governed legacy/external content or logged unresolved.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter presents invariants as review obligations, not a proof that satisfying them yields a correct architecture.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents semantic set interpretations and review predicates but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed conformance, compatibility, satisfaction, verification, pass, validation, migration equivalence, interoperability, correctness and performance language for evidence scope.
The executable checker is repeatedly labeled as a declared subset and explicitly cannot establish OMG conformance, correct requirements, physical adequacy, execution or system pass.
Formal-standard currency claims are tied to current official catalog/specification pages and distinguish adoption date from publication document date.
NASA-HDBK-1009A is identified as useful process evidence using a v1-era companion tool, not a normative source for SysML 2.0 syntax.
API, exchange and transformation success are never generalized to lossless interoperability or semantic equivalence without declared fixtures and evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external review or real-system empirical validation is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked SysML, KerML, language stack, model, notation, method, tool, architecture description, namespace/package/import, definition/usage, identity/name/version, typing, specialization, subsetting, redefinition, parts/items/ports, connections/interfaces/flows, actions/states/calculations/constraints, requirements/cases, concerns/viewpoints/views/renderings, metadata, authored/derived facts, API services, interchange and migration. Categories remain distinct and use final 2.0 concepts rather than v1 diagram taxonomy as the organizing frame.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked version baselining, durable package authority, import control, configured usage modeling, interaction contracts, cross-concern semantics, requirement and evidence lifecycle, audience-specific generated views, extension governance, semantic queries, API failure handling, round-trip fixtures, v1 transformation and risk-ranked cutover. Cases cover rail assets, clinical staffing, power interfaces, drone behavior, thermal margins, test evidence, stakeholder views, CI queries, tool exchange and satellite migration.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from the language/evidence boundary through foundational semantics, structure/behavior/requirements/views, query/API/interchange and migration. The one-page review supports retrieval; ten examples expose common category errors; five exercises and complete solutions require model design, audit, viewpoint governance, interoperability evaluation and migration planning with explicit limitations.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external OMG conformance assessment, academic review, SysML/KerML language-expert review, tool-vendor review, practicing systems-engineer review, domain/architecture review, physical-interface review, safety/security/assurance review, transformation/interoperability certification, verification/validation review, or decision-authority acceptance is claimed.
